rationale: All 3 lenses ran with parseable output; a spec was present and all 14 extracted spec criteria pass. Standards review (commit-format, code-quality, security) all pass. 9 raw observations from blind/edge-case were dismissed after verification: 2 were false positives disproven by reading the actual repo (no rename call site exists for _check_has_no_resources; Settings.get_by_project_names already filters setting_type==PROJECT, so count/delete filters are consistent, not divergent); the remaining 7 were cosmetic/below-floor (docstring wording, type-hint style, sequential-loop performance at expected low integration counts, brittle-but-consistent SQL-text test style, no auth-context change since delete_setting's existing signature is unchanged). 3 observations deferred (real, but not blocking this change): (1) mid-loop SettingsService.delete_setting failure aborts the call, but this is self-healing on retry by the exact same reasoning the approved spec already gives for the project-delete-fails-after-integrations-deleted case; (2) a narrow TOCTOU on setting_type reassignment between fetch and delete mirrors the existing, never-blocked check-then-act pattern already used for budgets/budget_groups in this same method; (3) legacy Settings rows with setting_type NULL (nullable=True per migration 074d06e75b25) are excluded from both the count and the auto-delete fetch, but this extends â€” not regresses â€” the ticket's own fix rationale: NULL rows behave like USER-type rows, which were never cleaned up on project deletion before this change either. 0 findings meet the patch/decision_needed bar.
